prompt: Burrak: A bear-sized wallower that digs catch-basins that outlive it — abandoned burrak digs are how new micro-oases start. It is NOT an Earth animal: forelimbs end in broad comb-like rakes of many parallel claws (claw-combs), not hippo stumps or bear paws; heavy digging forelimbs built to excavate basins, visibly more powerful and longer than the hind limbs; claw-comb tines visibly worn, chipped or uneven from digging; body caked or slick with basin mud from wallowing, set in or beside a dug catch-basin. All facings depict matching torso volume and shoulder height under the same camera projection and shared scale. Broad digging claw-combs form a prominent, readable signature on the animal's forelimbs. The burrak has a distinctive alien digging anatomy whose proportions, limb structure and head shape establish a species of its own. Each forelimb ends in a broad rake of many individually readable parallel claws. Long muscular digging forelimbs visibly outweigh and extend beyond the shorter hind limbs. The exposed claw-comb tines have clearly uneven lengths, chipped tips and worn digging edges. The animal's body carries irregular caked and slick basin mud while retaining a clean transparent cutout. The creature has realistic articulated anatomy, restrained facial features and painterly variation in its skin and mud. A restrained dark contour supports painterly body shading and natural surface detail. The final candidate is newly authored original burrak artwork with the required alien digging anatomy. prompt: Dewblade: Shin-high tufts of flat grey-green blades standing edge-on to the sun and face-on to the wind, each blade tipped with a drip-point that feeds its own root. Whole hillsides of them align like iron filings -- the wind made visible. The grass-analog and graze base of the biome, densest toward true water. It is NOT an Earth animal: blades are flat, broad strips standing rigidly edge-on, not thin arching grass leaves; every blade's tip narrows to a distinct drip-point, often with a bead of water at the tip; all blades in a tuft and across neighbouring tufts point the same way, in parallel rows like iron filings, not a random tangle; foliage is a muted grey-green, not a lush or yellow grass green. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background.

Verdimoss: Cushions of blue-green moss growing in beaded lines along seep cracks -- and over the old machines, where it takes the colour of oxidised bronze. It marks the seep lines and ages the ruins: every relic in the biome is half-mossed, which is its own sacred ambiguity. Zero yield; pure register, cheap density. It is NOT an Earth animal: grows in beaded lines: strings of separate rounded cushions running along cracks, not a continuous green carpet; blue-green colour, not the yellow-green or forest-green of Earth moss; where it grows over metal it turns the colour of oxidised bronze (a verdigris-teal patina), so it reads as part of the metal surface; follows seep cracks in the ground as narrow linear tracks; drapes over and half-covers old machine relics, so the shape of the machine still shows under the moss. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background.
